newsitem.title: UK: Topps Tiles jumps to premium on LSE debut.
newsitem.headline: Topps Tiles jumps to premium on LSE debut.

text.p: Shares in UK specialist tile retailer Topps Tiles Plc jumped to a 10.5 per cent premium on Monday in the first day of dealings on the London Stock Exchange.
The shares, issued at 100p, gained 10-1/2p to 110-1/2p by 1239 GMT in volume of 768,000 shares.
"We have seen a nice bit of two-way trade," said one dealer. "We weren't expecting fireworks but it has started well," he added.

Topps Tiles, valued at around 20 million stg at the issue price, is one of the largest specialist tile retailers in England and Wales, with 54 branches and plans to double the number of stores operated by the group over the next three years.

The company said it aimed to become the leading retail brand in the UK tile market, which market research for the industry estimates to be worth 160 million stg and forecast to grow by 21 per cent a year.
In the 53 weeks to June 1, 1996 Topps Tiles made a pre-tax profit of two million stg. It forecast profits for the year ending May 13, 1997 would not be less than 2.45 million stg.
